item.description: Oct 28, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey (0) dribbles the ball while Indiana Pacers guard Quenton Jackson (29) defends in the first half at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Here’s what I saw. The Sixers’ offense has not been good enough I don’t think I’m speaking out of turn when I say that this offense has been wildly disappointing to start the year. Nobody expects Philly to run a Warriors-esque motion offense or eschew isolation possessions entirely, but there is a lot of standing around and slamming of heads into walls. They are fortunate to have heads made of steel, but that doesn’t mean they can’t add variety and clean up the game plan. The only good news is that Joel Embiid — the iso-heavy hub at the center of the attack — has done a pretty damn good job of playing with a sense of urgency inside the arc, whether that has been attacking as a scorer or playing setup man for the rest of the group. He had his best scoring stretch of the season in the first half against Indiana, wasting almost no time or footsteps to get to his spots, rise up, and hit jumpers. The Sixers found him at spots all over the floor, attacking from deep post spots as well as his pick-and-roll comfort area at the nail, and he was quicker to rise and fire than we’d seen in his previous three appearances this season. That decisiveness created opportunities for the others around him, as the Pacers needed to respond to an Embiid touch quickly or risk giving him an immediate clean look. As Indiana converged around him, Embiid started a few swing pass sequences that saw the ball ping from LeBron James to VJ Edgecombe to Tyrese Maxey and to others in the rotation, and some of those plays ended up back in the hands of Embiid, who drew fouls on an undersized Indy frontline hanging onto him whenever possible. Embiid tends to be the hardest guy to figure out a style of play around for new players, so it’s encouraging to see them already hitting him on a high percentage of plays when he has established deep position. LeBron has been a cheat code in this regard. item.title: Suarez scores, Messi frustrated and Casemiro steadies the back line as Inter Miami rescue 2-2 draw with Cincinnati
item.description: Inter Miami CF v FC Cincinnati - Getty Images Sport Inter Miami CF and FC Cincinnati played out a pulsating 2-2 draw at Nu Stadium, with all four goals coming in the second half. Luis Suarez opened the scoring from a Casemiro assist, before a rapid Cincinnati comeback was cancelled out by Riquelme Fillipi in the 90th minute. The air at Nu Stadium was thick with expectation as Inter Miami CF and FC Cincinnati met with plenty at stake for both sides. Miami, third in the Eastern Conference and led by Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez, wanted to bounce back from a defeat at the New York Red Bulls. Cincinnati arrived chasing a playoff place and needing points. The first half was cagey, with both sides prioritising defensive solidity, and it ended 0-0. Messi was booked in the 44th minute. Suarez breaks the deadlock after cagey opening The match came alive in the 61st minute when Luis Suarez reminded everyone of his predatory instincts. Casemiro supplied the assist, and the Uruguayan finished to give the Herons a lead that settled the home crowd. Miami had made two changes at the break, with Telasco Segovia and Ian Fray replacing Matías Galarza and Sergio Reguilón. They grew in confidence and began to dominate. Cincinnati turn the tide in dramatic fashion Just as Miami looked to be cruising toward a narrow win, the match took a chaotic turn. Cincinnati, who had stayed disciplined, struck back through Kenji Mboma Dem in the 80th minute, set up by Evander, to silence the Florida crowd. Only six minutes later, Samuel Gidi turned the game on its head, finishing from a Tyler Barlow assist to put the visitors 2-1 ahead. Fillipi provides the final twist With defeat looming, Inter Miami threw caution to the wind. Riquelme Fillipi, who had come on in the 83rd minute for Germán Berterame, was the hero. In the 90th minute he took Rodrigo De Paul’s delivery in a crowded penalty area and finished to make it 2-2. The goal set off wild celebrations on the Miami bench and secured a result that felt fair given how the game had gone. Key performers and tactical shifts Suarez and Fillipi grabbed the headlines for the hosts, with Casemiro’s assist for the opener a reminder of his influence from the back. Messi had a quieter night. He was booked just before the break and saw a shot blocked in the second half. For Cincinnati, fresh legs including Barlow and T. Anunga helped them exploit a tiring Miami defence. Despite the flurry of goals, Miami’s discipline was questioned as they picked up three yellow cards: Messi at 44', Segovia at 90+3' and Suarez at 90+4'. Implications for the Eastern Conference race The draw keeps Inter Miami in a strong position in the top three of the Eastern Conference, though they will regret the defensive lapses that let Cincinnati back into the contest. For FC Cincinnati, the point is a testament to their fighting spirit and keeps their playoff hopes alive. item.title: Florence Motor Speedway’s Future Highlights the Challenges Facing Short Track Racing
item.description: A light rain falls during super late model qualifying while sportsman cars wait on pit road Florence Motor Speedway’s announcement that it will not race in 2027 is the latest reminder of how difficult it has become to keep local short tracks operating. But while some facilities are closing, others are investing millions to bring racing back. The South Carolina track cited increasing operating costs, declining car counts, and lower fan attendance as reasons behind its decision. Florence has hosted major Late Model events, including the South Carolina 400, and attracted NASCAR drivers such as Dale Earnhardt Jr. since its current ownership took over in 2020. Florence isn’t alone. California’s Irwindale Speedway closed in December 2024 after 25 years, while Ontario’s Sunset Speedway ended racing following the 2025 season. A redevelopment proposal for Sunset would replace the racetrack with more than 1,200 self-storage units. However, not every short track is facing the same outcome. Former NASCAR driver Matt Tifft purchased Mansfield Speedway in Ohio and invested millions into reopening the facility in 2026 after seven years without racing. The track returned in May with a sold-out opening event and a schedule extending beyond racing to concerts and other entertainment. The contrast highlights the challenges facing track operators. Rising expenses and smaller fields can make traditional weekly racing difficult to sustain, while larger investments and additional events may offer another approach. For drivers, fewer local tracks can mean longer trips and higher costs to compete. For fans, closures eliminate opportunities to watch grassroots racing close to home. Florence plans to finish its 2026 schedule before pausing operations. Whether racing eventually returns remains uncertain, but its situation raises a question facing short tracks nationwide: what will it take to keep them open?

item.description: Manchester City 2-2 Brighton [4-3p]: City beat Seagulls 4-3 on penalties in close cup tie Holders Manchester City hosted Brighton at a noticeably empty Etihad Stadium in round four of the EFL Cup, off the back of their first league loss of the season against Aston Villa on Saturday. Brighton came into the fourth round having lost five of their six previous fourth round matches in the EFL Cup, with the only outlier being a third round loss to Chelsea. A win would see their strong start to the season continue despite their 2-0 loss away to Liverpool at the weekend. As it happened Both sides fielded XIs with a mix of junior and senior players and started out working swiftly on the counter, with Brighton’s Michael Svoboda lucky not to concede a penalty early on against Rayan Cherki as he took him down on the edge of the box with inches to spare. The visitors got off the mark first on the stroke of 30 minutes as Jack Hinshelwood played the ball into the box to Georginio Rutter who shot from distance, but it was directed in by 20-year-old Malick Yalcouye, who clipped the ball into the right-hand side of the goal where it was spilled by City goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli into the back of the net. Manchester City equalised just nine minutes later through Mateo Kovacic after loose Brighton defending gave away possession in a dangerous area. Floyd Samba’s clip into the box hit the arm of Jaouen Hadjam but Phil Foden carried on playing, keeping his composure as his teammates stopped to call for handball allowing Kovacic to shoot from outside of the box and put it past Jason Steele to make it 1-1. There is no VAR at this stage of the competition, meaning play could not be called back. Brighton came out swinging for the second half as Hadjam broke forward on the left wing and then cut back in the box to Rutter who placed his shot into the bottom right corner with ease to give Fabian Hurzeler’s side their lead back within two minutes of kick-off. They tried to make the most of their advantage, pinning Enzo Maresca’s men back into their own half but failed to make the most of any corners or chances. City took the opportunity from a counter to push play back into Brighton’s half and after Rutter conceded a foul on Foden inside the D, equalised from a Cherki free kick in the 72nd minute, which was deflected into goal past Steele by his teammate Vitor Reis to make it 2-2. Hurzeler’s decision to bring on Lewis Dunk, one of his most reliable penalty takers, was telling of how he planned to use the game’s final 10 minutes. Maresca followed suit minutes later, bringing on Enzo Fernandez. Although both had their fair share of chances, the final score in normal time was 2-2. With no extra time in this stage of the cup it was straight to spot kicks and after six perfect penalties it was Kovacic to fall first, shooting low into the arms of Steele, but he was quickly redeemed as Yasin Ayari took a near-identical kick that was also saved, failing to give Brighton any lead. item.title: Kane denies Ballon d'Or quote was aimed at Mbappé and Yamal: "A quote I've loved my whole career"
item.description: Kane denies Ballon d'Or quote was aimed at Mbappé and Yamal: "A quote I've loved my whole career" ( Allianz Arena, München ) Fresh off winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or award in London, Harry Kane was in fine form as he took a back seat for Bayern Munich's 6-1 win over 1.FC Magdeburg in the second round of the DFB-Pokal tonight. "It was a crazy week. What an unbelievable night on Monday [at the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London]. There was a lot of waiting around and trying to picture what it would be like to win," Kane told Bulinews.com and other media present in the mixed zone. "It's really special, the support I've had from friends, family and fans. It's just been almost overwhelming. I had a good night with ones close to me and now it's just straight back to work and take it all in. "I could have played tonight but Danksy said he was trying to give me a break in this game. We have played a lot of games lately and he was thinking about bringing me on, but then we scored the fourth goal and killed the game off," he explained. Kane, who posted the quote 'work hard in silence, let success be your noise' after his Ballon d'Or triumph, but the 33-year-old was quick to deny whether it was directed at his nearest competitors Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal. "No, not at all, this is a quote I've loved throughout my whole career to be honest. It amplifies me, what I do, and how I approach hard work, discipline and dedication. Many times I have had to train on my own. "Behind the scenes, all the work that I do. I just think it's a great quote and one that lots of boys and girls can look at and use to help them as well," the striker said, offering advice to those who look up to him as an idol. Asked about Saturday's Bundesliga meeting with top-of-the-table Borussia Dortmund, the Englishman said he is already looking forward to the test and a chance to pull clear of their rivals at the summit. "It's a big match, it's going to be the biggest of the season in the Bundesliga so far. We know how much of a boost it will be to win and go three points clear. So, hopefully we can finish the week on a high this Saturday," he concluded.

item.title: Newcomers shine in MSU women's basketball's exhibition win
item.description: EAST LANSING — Newcomers Monique Bobongie and Carter McCray each had big performances to help the Michigan State women's basketball team wins its tune-up for the season. Bobongie had a game-high 21 points and McCray added 20 points off the bench for the Spartans in a 100-53 victory over Michigan Tech on Wednesday, Oct. 28 at Breslin Center. Bobongie, a freshman from Australia, added seven rebounds and was 9-of-14 from the field. McCray, a transfer from West Virginia, was 8-of-9 shooting from the floor. McCray and Bobongie were among five players in double figures scoring for the Spartans. Kennedy Blair had 13 points, Tabitha Betson scored 12 points and Theryn Hallock added 11 points. Michigan Tech had two players in double figures, which included East Lansing graduate Soraya Timms finishing with 13 points. MSU's Lilly Williams sits Freshman and McDonald's All-American Lilly Williams didn't play in the exhibition for MSU. The former Howell standout and Michigan Miss Basketball winner just returned to practice Tuesday, Oct. 27 following eye surgery. MSU coach Robyn Fralick is hopeful Williams will play in the Spartans' season opener against Valparaiso on Tuesday, Nov. 3. "We'll be excited to get her going full speed too," Fralick said. item.title: New Trade Destination Emerges For Vikings’ Jauan Jennings Ahead Of Week 8
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Jauan Jennings #14 of the Minnesota Vikings catches a pass against the Indianapolis Colts in the second quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty Vikings receiver Jauan Jennings entered this season with high expectations to develop into a key weapon as Minnesota’s third receiver. After all, they signed him to a one-year, $8 million deal this offseason to be just that. Unfortunately, it’d be an understatement to say the season hasn’t gone as planned for the pass-catcher. He has only four catches for 43 yards. He’s on pace for 122 receiving yards, which would be the lowest of his career by a wide margin. Jennings also had an emotional outburst on the sidelines during the team’s Week 5 matchup against New Orleans. With him struggling to carve out a role in Minnesota’s offense, many believe he’s a strong trade candidate ahead of the November 10 trade deadline. The 49ers are probably the most common landing spot for Jennings, as he spent the first six years of his career in San Francisco and they’ve had a run of bad luck with injuries at receiver. Meanwhile, others have mentioned the Rams as a possible destination after Davante Adams landed on Injured Reserve with a hamstring injury. Interestingly, a new team has emerged as a potential landing spot: The defending AFC Champion New England Patriots . BleacherReport ‘s Kristopher Knox listed them as one of two teams (along with the 49ers) that could trade for Jennings. He also mentioned they might be willing to make a deal if they can find a running back in return. “The Minnesota Vikings are the last remaining undefeated team, but they could still consider moving an expendable piece to address an area of need,” Knox wrote. “Specifically, they might try to add a running back, as Aaron Jones continues to deal with an MCL sprain . “If Jennings can bring backfield depth or draft capital that can be used to find it, Minnesota might be convinced to make a deal. Jennings, who had 643 yards and nine touchdowns last season, would be worth it to a receiver-needy team.” What Could The Vikings Get For Jennings? The Vikings probably wouldn’t expect much in terms of draft compensation for the disgruntled pass-catcher. Not with him playing out a one-year deal, anyway. Whoever takes him on would have to either re-sign him or acquire him knowing he’ll be a two-month rental. However, a player-for-player trade actually would make a lot of sense for the disgruntled pass-catcher. If the Vikings hoped to bolster their running back room as Knox suggested, they’d probably find common ground much easier there. item.title: Rams don’t have an impressive win on resume
item.description: Seven weeks into the season and it’s still unclear exactly who the Los Angeles Rams are this year. They lost to the 49ers in a weird season opener with international travel as a confounding variable. LA also dropped close games to the Denver Broncos, Buffalo Bills, and Arizona Cardinals. Arizona aside, that’s three losses to teams who figure into the playoff picture for their respective conferences. Add in the wins and things get even more confusing. The Rams beat the New York Giants in Week 2. Jaxson Dart was injured early. Jameis Winston was inept in replacement, and he’s since been replaced in the starting lineup by JJ McCarthy. LA defeated the Philadelphia Eagles prior to them falling off a cliff. In Week 4 they were missing DeVonta Smith, Zack Baun, Dallas Goedert, and Lane Johnson entering the game. Saquon Barkley exited early and did not return. Part of the subsequent downfall of Philadelphia is attributable to Jalen Hurts’ absence, but it’s fair to question whether the Eagles were a good team before all their attrition. And then there are the Raiders, who started the season 3-0 before falling to 3-4 following last weekend’s loss to the Rams. The fact that Las Vegas is encouraged by a 3-4 start tells you they didn’t expect to compete much this season. While the Rams handled them solidly, the Raiders did show life in the second half. Overall, in one way to read it, we can say the Rams lost to the 1-4 Cardinals and then bounced back against a bad Raiders team. Their two other wins aren’t anything to hang their hat on either. The Rams have yet to beat a good team. That may be an overly pessimistic view. It certainly does not tell the whole story. The difficult truth is we might not know who the Rams truly are for some time. Wins over the Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders, and Arizona Cardinals in the next three weeks for the bye don’t move the needle. Losing to these teams could confirm that LA isn’t as good as they expected to be entering the year. The Rams host the Green Bay Packers the day before Thanksgiving and then the Chiefs the following week. They have games to follow against the 49ers and Cowboys before seeing the Seahawks in two out of the three final games of the regular season. We might not know who the Rams are until the final moments before the playoffs. The coming weeks can only prove they are a pretender. Establishing themselves as a contender must come later. The encouraging news is that the Rams, if they can make it to the bye week unscathed, should expect reinforcements coming out of their bye before their schedule grows more competitive. Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson, Davante Adams, Kobie Turner, and others could potentially return in time for the daunting finale. Beating the Giants, Eagles, and Raiders doesn’t tell me who you are. We won’t truly learn much about the Rams until the calendar turns from November into December and thereafter.

item.title: Why NASCAR Drivers Are Racing Nitrous Powered Crown Vics at the Freedom Factory
item.description: Late model Ford Crown Victorias race past the main grandstand Denny Hamlin, Carson Hocevar, and Ryan Preece are trading their usual race cars for nitrous powered Ford Crown Victorias at Cleetus McFarland’s Freedom Factory in Bradenton, Florida. The 2.4 Hours of LeMullets returns November 13, bringing NASCAR drivers, celebrities, and internet personalities together for a endurance race featuring two driver teams and a mandatory driver change. For some drivers, this isn’t their first experience racing Crown Vics. Hocevar teamed up with McFarland to win the 2025 LeMullets event, while Preece previously won a Crown Vic race at Stafford Speedway. The 2026 lineup also includes Ty Dillon, Hailie Deegan, T-Pain, Vanilla Ice, and actor Dax Shepard, creating an unusual mix of professional racers and entertainers. The Freedom Factory has its own motorsports history. Formerly DeSoto Speedway, the facility was revived by McFarland after years of inactivity and has since become a destination for unconventional racing events. But LeMullets isn’t just about recognizable names. Drivers still have to navigate traffic, manage their cars, and execute a driver swap while competing for the win. The race begins November 13 at 7:30 p.m. Eastern, with live coverage on FRDM+.

item.description: Copyright: xJonxEndowx JonxEndowx iosphotos389463 ©IMAGO/Newscom World The WNBA and the NBA have taken different approaches to preparing college basketball players for the professional level. While NBA-bound prospects have had the opportunity to leave college early for decades, the WNBA continues to operate under eligibility restrictions that determine when American players can turn professional. But do these rules still reflect the realities of today’s women’s basketball landscape? For JuJu Watkins’ USC teammate Jazzy Davidson, they may be a little outdated. Davidson, who is preparing for her sophomore season with the Trojans, was asked in an October 28 interview with Baker Machado of Front Office Sports whether players should have the option to turn professional earlier. Her response reflected the complexity of the issue. “I definitely think that the eligibility rules right now are maybe a little bit outdated,” she said. “But there is something to say in the college experience in my opinion. I love the NCAA, I love college sports. I love going to school here at USC, getting an education, forming those relationships with my teammates. So, yeah, I’d have to think more on that, but it’s hard for me to say.” Her answer reflected both sides of the debate. While the USC guard acknowledged that the current system may need reconsideration, she also made it clear that the college experience offers something valuable beyond basketball. The WNBA's eligibility debate just got fiercer from inside the college game. Subscribe to stay ahead of how this conversation reshapes women's basketball's future. Unlike its men’s counterpart, which has allowed college players to enter the professional ranks before completing four years of eligibility for more than 50 years, the WNBA maintains specific requirements that limit when American players can enter its draft. Under the league’s collective bargaining agreement with the WNBPA, college players must meet at least one of several eligibility criteria. A player can qualify by graduating from a four-year college within three months of the draft, being four years removed from high school graduation, or turning at least 22 during the calendar year in which the draft takes place. Eligible players with remaining NCAA eligibility can then renounce it and declare for the WNBA Draft. International prospects face a different age requirement. They must turn at least 20 during the calendar year of the draft to become eligible, allowing for a distinction between the pathways available to American college players and international prospects. item.description: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli needs just two points at the Mexican Grand Prix to become the youngest-ever world champion and the first Italian to take the title in 73 years (RONALDO SCHEMIDT) Kimi Antonelli will take his place in Formula One’s record books as the youngest champion and Italy’s first since 1953, barring a wild swing of unexpected misfortunes amid a fiesta atmosphere at this weekend’s Mexico City Grand Prix. The runaway leader of the drivers’ championship needs to finish ninth or better in his Mercedes to take the title aged 20 years and 68 days, lowering the record held by Sebastian Vettel by more than three years. Almost more remarkably, he will also succeed Italy's last champion Alberto Ascari, who won for Ferrari in 1953, after a gap of 73 years during which his country has become synonymous with Formula One. After winning the United States Grand Prix last Sunday, his two remaining title rivals team-mate George Russell and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton are 123 and 124 points adrift respectively and can only prevent the seemingly inevitable by winning and hoping Antonelli finishes 10th or worse. Such an outcome is highly unlikely. Antonelli has won nine races of this year’s 18 to date. In his last 11, he has scored nine podium finishes, one fifth and one 15th place – only his second non-points-scoring race in 18 outings that began with a second-place in Australia followed by five wins. It is the consistency of a champion, a driver with a clear vision of his work and a cool head albeit on such young shoulders. Out of the car, he is boyish, precocious and has an infectious sense of fun. Some have said he behaves like a puppy. But when the visor is pulled down, he has proved he has both the talent and the mentality to win and remain, mostly, unflappable under pressure. “I’m going to approach it with the same mindset,” he said in Texas. “Trying to have as much fun as possible, but trying to fight for another win.
